alreadyObserved: The official RWTH record, its two-page metadata document, the associated primary paper text, and the official GitLab project landing page were inspected.

The source reports 48 same-lot commercial C-grade Sanyo/Panasonic UR18650E NMC/graphite cells aged with one common profile at 25 degrees Celsius, with four-cell start batches shifted by two to three days.
The source reports a BOL characterization followed by periodic RPTs, including capacity and pulse-resistance tests at approximately 70%, 50%, and 30% SOC.

The paper states that testing continued beyond 80% EOL, that the mean EOL80 was approximately 1175 cycles, that there were about 17 characterization rounds per cell, and that one cell had an incomplete degradation curve.
The official repository master commit was 488eb68c23898f46308f58b9299088c287b9380d at sealing.
notYetObservedAtSeal: No raw or processed cell-level result file from the RWTH dataset was cloned, downloaded, opened, parsed, plotted, or summarized.
No cell-level BOL capacity, first-RPT capacity, 30%-SOC pulse resistance, EOL cycle, censoring time, prediction, error, or hypothesis verdict was observed.
No target outcome informed the split, feature definitions, model, thresholds, missingness rule, or decision gates.

selection.reason: RC54 showed that imposed stress can rank pooled lifetime while early diagnostic changes did not recover triplicate ordering. The RWTH experiment removes the stress-confounding escape route: all 48 cells share chemistry, lot, temperature, and cycling profile, while BOL and repeated capacity and pulse tests precede a recorded 80% EOL. It therefore directly tests whether a sparse early response identifies cell-specific frailty under fixed conditions.
selection.claimBoundary: RC55 tests cell-to-cell ordering in one C-grade NMC/graphite lot under one laboratory profile. It cannot establish chemistry transfer, temperature transfer, field-duty transfer, pack RUL, safety, warranty, or a universal digital twin.
selection.deferredScope: Cyber-trust experiments, new battery cycling, destructive analysis, field packs, operational safety decisions, and claims beyond the public RWTH cohort remain outside scope.

sourceManifest.license: CC BY 4.0 for the dataset, as stated by the official metadata
sourceManifest.cellType: Sanyo/Panasonic UR18650E commercial C-grade NMC/graphite cylindrical cell
sourceManifest.cohort: 48 cells from one production lot, aged under one profile at 25 degrees Celsius
sourceManifest.resultIntegrity: After acquisition, record repository commit, source paths, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes before parsing. Any mismatch from the sealed commit stops interpretation until documented.

cohortAndSplit.identifierRule: Use the source's integer cell number from 1 through 48. If source identifiers cannot be mapped bijectively to these integers without reading outcomes, stop and document the schema failure.
inclusionRule: Include all 48 source cells before inspecting completeness or EOL.
Require a resolvable BOL capacity record, first post-aging RPT capacity record, and their cycle or charge-throughput positions for the capacity-response arm.
Require resolvable 30%-SOC 10 ms discharge-pulse resistance at both BOL and first post-aging RPT for the pulse-response arm.
Define an observed event only from a registered 80%-of-own-BOL capacity crossing; otherwise retain the cell as right-censored at its last resolvable capacity observation.
Do not remove a cell because its response, lifetime, residual, or trajectory is extreme.

pilot.use: Exact file paths, delimiters, units, cycle index, BOL/RPT identity, capacity field, pulse direction, pulse duration, and 30%-SOC mapping only.
pilot.permittedAmendment: Before any non-pilot row is read, one dated amendment may map exact source columns and file keys to the quantities already registered here or declare a quantity unavailable. It may not change the split, endpoint, feature meaning, model, thresholds, or hypotheses.

development.rule: After removing pilot cells 1 and 2, source cell number not divisible by 3.

untouchedTarget.reason: The arithmetic split is fixed before cell-level results and distributes the four-cell start batches across development and target without outcome-aware selection.

endpointContract.landmark: The source cycle or equivalent-full-cycle position of the first post-aging RPT used to form both response coordinates.
endpointContract.capacityReference: The same cell's BOL 2 A discharge capacity, using the source's standardized capacity-test definition.
endpointContract.event: The first later standardized capacity observation at or below 0.80 times that cell's BOL reference capacity.
endpointContract.eventTime: Cycles from the response landmark to the first observed threshold-crossing capacity observation.
endpointContract.censorTime: If no crossing is observed, cycles from the response landmark to the last later standardized capacity observation.
endpointContract.resolution: No interpolation between RPT capacity observations and no reuse of partial aging-cycle turnover as a full-capacity label.
endpointContract.prohibitedInterpretation: The endpoint is an interval-resolved electrochemical capacity threshold, not a physical failure, hazard, warranty, or pack-level retirement event.

baselineArm.definition: A development-cohort lifetime distribution with no cell-specific predictor.

capacityResponseArm.definition: log(Q_first_RPT/Q_BOL) divided by the positive cycle or equivalent-full-cycle distance between those two standardized capacity measurements.

pulseResponseArm.definition: log(R10ms_first_RPT/R10ms_BOL) divided by the positive cycle or equivalent-full-cycle distance between the paired 30%-SOC discharge-pulse measurements. This is the only pulse coordinate permitted.

rowRules: Prefer processed source quantities only when the official code exposes their derivation; otherwise derive them from raw current-voltage-time rows with the same published procedure.
Map 30% SOC by the source's explicit SOC field or by the published voltage-to-SOC characterization mapping, never by inspecting association with EOL.
For a discharge pulse, compute R10ms as the signed voltage drop divided by the signed current step and require a finite positive result in ohms or converted milliohms.
If multiple valid observations represent one cell, round, SOC, and pulse duration, use their median before forming the response.
Every logarithm input and exposure interval must be finite and strictly positive.
featureContract.preprocessing: For B and C separately, subtract the non-pilot development mean and divide by the non-pilot development population standard deviation. Replace an exactly zero development standard deviation with one. Pilot and target rows have zero influence.
featureContract.missingness: No imputation, target-derived centering, clipping, proxy substitution, or outcome-aware repair. Fit each arm on development cells complete for that arm and score only target cells complete for that arm; report exact denominators and missing fields.
featureContract.coverageGate: Each active response arm must retain at least 90% of its 16 target candidates.

modelContract.model: Separate penalized Weibull accelerated-failure-time model for A, B, and C. log(lambda_i)=intercept+x_i beta; each arm has its own shared Weibull shape k.
modelContract.likelihood: Use the right-censored Weibull likelihood in remaining cycles from the first post-aging RPT. Penalize beta, but not intercept or log(k), by fixed L2 alpha 1.0.
modelContract.initialization: Intercept equals log of the development median observed-or-censor time, beta is zero, and log(k)=log(2).
modelContract.optimizer: Primary Python uses deterministic BFGS. A separately written dependency-free Node implementation repeats extraction from the sealed feature table and fits the same likelihood. No target calibration, feature selection, hyperparameter search, ensemble, or outcome-driven restart is allowed.
modelContract.prediction: Predicted remaining median cycles equals lambda_i times (log 2)^(1/k). Predicted survival at horizon t equals exp(-(t/lambda_i)^k).
modelContract.independentTolerance: Absolute disagreement at most 1e-5 for every target prediction and scalar metric; hypothesis verdicts must match exactly.

metricContract.ranking: Harrell concordance over target cells; a pair is comparable when the shorter observed time is an event. Tied prediction receives half credit.
metricContract.sameConditionDenominator: All target cells share the same chemistry, lot, temperature, and aging profile. Report the exact comparable-pair count and require at least 30 pairs for a frailty-ranking claim.
metricContract.calibration: At 900 and 1100 remaining cycles after the response landmark, compare mean predicted survival with target Kaplan-Meier survival and report absolute error and at-risk count.
metricContract.pairedImprovement: Among target cells with observed events and paired predictions, report (A MdAE - B or C MdAE)/A MdAE and C-versus-B change. Use 2000 seeded bootstrap resamples of target cells with seed 55029; intervals are descriptive and cannot rescue a failed gate.
metricContract.reporting: Publish every target prediction, event/censor flag, start batch when recoverable, both registered features, and every registered metric even when a gate fails.

competingHypotheses.claim: A common-condition lifetime distribution is sufficient; the two early responses do not identify stable cell-specific frailty.
competingHypotheses.retain: Retain if neither H1 nor H2 satisfies every success condition.

competingHypotheses.claim: The first-RPT capacity response identifies cell-specific EOL ordering under fixed stress.
competingHypotheses.success: Arm B has at least 90% target coverage, at least 14 target events and 30 comparable pairs, Harrell concordance at least 0.65, median absolute error at most 160 cycles, at least 10% MdAE improvement over A, and maximum 900/1100-cycle calibration error at most 0.15.

competingHypotheses.claim: The 30%-SOC 10 ms pulse-resistance response supplies frailty information beyond the capacity response.
competingHypotheses.success: Arm C has at least 90% target coverage, at least 14 target events and 30 comparable pairs, Harrell concordance at least 0.70, median absolute error at most 140 cycles, at least 10% MdAE improvement over B, no worse calibration error than B, and independent reproduction within tolerance.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if any boundary fails; pooled fit or a favorable coefficient sign cannot substitute for held-cell ordering, calibration, coverage, or independent reproduction.

causalChain: One lot and one imposed aging profile plus standardized BOL and first-RPT measurements
latent manufacturing susceptibility that stress descriptors cannot explain
a preregistered early capacity response and at most one 30%-SOC 10 ms pulse-resistance response
untouched same-condition EOL time, right censoring, calibration, and pairwise ordering
retain or reject sparse early electrochemical response as a cell-frailty bridge
fastFailureTests: If the official repository cannot be pinned to the sealed commit or acquired files cannot be hashed, stop before parsing.

If pilot cells cannot establish BOL, first post-aging RPT, capacity units, 30%-SOC identity, discharge sign, or 10 ms duration without outcome-dependent judgment, amend once or declare the affected arm unavailable.
If fewer than 90% of target cells have an arm's features, that arm fails coverage and is reported without a predictive claim.
If fewer than 14 target EOL events or 30 comparable target pairs remain, H1 and H2 fail the denominator gate.
If Python and Node disagree beyond 1e-5, stop interpretation and debug before publication.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Use standardized source characterization rounds, one capacity response, one explicitly defined 30%-SOC 10 ms discharge-pulse response, and source-derived units.
uncertaintyBudget.residual: Pulse timing, fixture resistance, temperature equalization, and RPT interval may obscure a weak manufacturing signal.
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Unresolvable pulse duration, direction, SOC, or capacity-round identity makes the affected arm unavailable.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Freeze two scalar response coordinates, a nested Weibull AFT form, alpha, initialization, and gates before cell-level results; reproduce in an independent runtime.
uncertaintyBudget.residual: A linear log-scale frailty effect and one Weibull shape may be misspecified.
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Optimization failure, nonfinite parameters, or independent disagreement blocks a verdict.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Hold out 16 arithmetic-ID cells and keep pilot cells at zero model weight; report start-batch labels when recoverable.
uncertaintyBudget.residual: The cohort is one factory-selected C-grade lot, and cells began testing in four-cell batches separated by several days.
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Do not generalize beyond this lot or interpret start-batch confounding as intrinsic chemistry.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Use each cell's own BOL capacity, preserve right censoring, and avoid interpolation between RPTs.
uncertaintyBudget.residual: RPT spacing makes EOL interval-resolved, and own-BOL normalization differs from nominal-capacity retirement rules.
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Do not represent the endpoint as a physical failure or safety boundary.

uncertaintyBudget.control: Make only a same-condition held-cell claim and require ranking, absolute error, calibration, coverage, and independent reproduction together.
uncertaintyBudget.residual: No temperature, duty-cycle, chemistry, laboratory, grade, or pack transfer is tested.
uncertaintyBudget.stop: Any cross-domain claim requires a new preregistered source and untouched holdout.

minimalAcademicAdvance: A negative result with adequate target coverage will show whether early capacity fade and a single pulse-resistance response can or cannot order later EOL among nominally identical, same-stress NMC/graphite cells; this directly narrows the frailty signal that RC54 failed to recover across heterogeneous stress conditions.
safetyEthics: RC55 uses public, previously collected battery data. It performs no charging, cell opening, personal-data processing, security testing, or operational safety decision.
